standard_prerequisites.use: They define $F_{X/S} : X \to X^{(p)}$, show it is finite, and give the cartesian square expressing the Frobenius of an etale chart over the base.

standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness, flatness and the local complete intersection property give finite syntomic

standard_prerequisites.use: Flatness is checked on fibres through the criterion, the fibre map is flat because the source fibre is Cohen-Macaulay over the regular target, and with the lci property this makes $F_{X/S}$ finite syntomic, so that the Garel map $\Theta$ is available.

standard_prerequisites.name: Etale charts of a smooth morphism and the compatibility of $\Theta$ with base change
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms, label morphisms-lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space (invoked at proof line 4407), Etale Morphisms, label etale-lemma-relative-frobenius-etale (invoked at proof line 4422) and Same chapter derham.tex, label lemma-etale (invoked at proof line 4425)
standard_prerequisites.use: They provide an etale chart $U \to \mathbf{A}^d_S$ over which the Frobenius square is cartesian with the $p$-power map, so that $\Theta$ for $X$ is pulled back from $\Theta$ for affine space.

standard_prerequisites.name: The universal and complex computations of the Garel map
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter derham.tex, label example-Garel (invoked at proof line 4439)
standard_prerequisites.use: They allow the formula for $\Theta^i$ to be computed in the universal case over $\mathbf{Z}$ and, for the needed trace formula, in the complex case after inverting the coordinates.

core_obligations: Establish that $F_{X/S}$ is finite syntomic: finiteness from the basic properties of the relative Frobenius, flatness by the fibre criterion together with the Cohen-Macaulay-over-regular statement, and the local complete intersection property, which combines with flatness (proof lines 4383-4396).

Reduce the computation of $\Theta$ to affine space: choose an etale chart $U \to \mathbf{A}^d_S$ around a point, note that the Frobenius square is cartesian, and use compatibility of $\Theta$ with base change together with $\Omega_{U/S} = \pi^*\Omega_{\mathbf{A}^d_S/S}$ (proof lines 4398-4427).

Compute $\Theta^i$ for the $p$-power map of polynomial rings: reduce to the universal case over $\mathbf{Z}$ and further to the complex case after inverting the coordinates, use $\mathrm{d}x_i = p^{-1}x_i^{-p+1}\mathrm{d}y_i$ and the properties of $\Theta^i$ to obtain the trace formula, and evaluate the trace: it vanishes unless $e_1, \ldots, e_i \equiv -1$ and $e_{i+1}, \ldots, e_d \equiv 0$ modulo $p$, in which case the displayed monomial results (proof lines 4429-4475).
Conclude that the map is zero in characteristic $p$ unless $i = d$, and that in degree $d$ every form is hit, so the map is surjective there (proof lines 4476-4477).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to affine space via etale charts (proof lines 4398-4427).
Vanishing except in degree $d$ and surjectivity (proof lines 4476-4477).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the Garel map of the relative Frobenius of a smooth morphism in characteristic $p$: it vanishes in all degrees except the top one, where it is surjective (statement lines 4367-4380). The proof first shows the Frobenius is finite syntomic by checking flatness on fibres and using the lci property, then reduces the computation to affine space by etale charts and base change compatibility, and finally computes the map on the universal $p$-power map of polynomial rings through a trace formula obtained in the complex case, concluding the vanishing and the surjectivity. The explicit trace computation is the substance, so the claim is H2.
